clue.text: Running problem 11 does not have

parts.note: a sharp side pain is a runner's complaint, and a naked runner (the answer to 11) does not have a thread of clothing on

explanation.surface: A jogger's trouble that some other runner escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is STREAKER, a naked runner. A stitch is the cramp you get while running, and someone with 'not a stitch on' is wearing nothing, so the streaker has no stitch in the clothing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sudden side pain brought on by running, and also a single loop of sewing in a garment.

clue.text: Direct control

explanation.surface: Two words for being in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to direct affairs and to hold control over them, as a ruler or a machine regulator does.

clue.text: Well you will not be able to claim this

definitions.text: Well you will not be able to claim this

parts.words: Well you will not be able to claim this
parts.note: read 'Well' as 'in good health': a healthy person has no right to the state payment made to people too ill to work

explanation.surface: A grudging remark that some payment is out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a throat-clearing opener, but it means healthy. In Britain this was the state payment to people off work through illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The state allowance paid to someone off work through illness can only be claimed by the unwell.

clue.text: The French ostler finds space in the car

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
an ostler is a stableman who looks after horses, as a groom does

explanation.surface: A stableman from France finds room in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: An ostler was the man who looked after horses at an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the room for passengers' legs, a key comfort measure in a car's interior.

clue.text: Resolved a debatable point that placated the children

explanation.surface: Ending an argument that had upset the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is an old word for children or offspring, so calming them settles the issue in a second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle an issue is to decide a disputed matter; issue also means offspring, whom one might settle down.

clue.text: It is mainly to the east of America

definitions.text: It is mainly to the east of America

parts.words: It is mainly to the east of America
parts.note: 'mainly' hides 'main', the sea: the ocean that lies off the eastern shore of the United States

explanation.surface: A geography question about what lies chiefly east of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'for the most part', but the main is the open sea, and this ocean is east of America.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean between the Americas and Europe and Africa lies along the eastern coast of America.

clue.text: Spectators at an interview could be captive

explanation.surface: Onlookers at a questioning who might be held there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be captive' points to the phrase 'captive audience', people who cannot leave.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a group of onlookers, and also a formal meeting granted by an important person such as the Pope.

clue.text: A drink back in Spain contained poison

indicators.note: back says the word for the drink is read from its end to its start

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
taken as written
E is the international vehicle registration for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A drink brought back from Spain turned out to be laced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PORT into TROP; 'contained' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade, used in small doses in medicine.

clue.text: Picnic-in a restaurant?

explanation.surface: Is a picnic the same as dining in a restaurant?
explanation.walkthrough: A picnic is eating out of doors; dining in a restaurant is eating away from home. The same phrase covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a meal away from home, whether outdoors or at a restaurant, uses the same everyday phrase.

clue.text: Got the present

parts.note: read as grammar: the present tense of the verb whose past tense is 'got'

explanation.surface: Someone received a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' is not a gift but the present tense: 'got' turned into the present is this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The base, present-tense form of the verb whose past is 'got'.

clue.text: Runner barely visible

explanation.surface: An athlete hard to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means naked: someone who runs naked through a public place is seen in the bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who dashes naked through a crowd is seen bare, and also a fast mover, like a streak of light.

clue.text: Sad model with soldier in broken-down car

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car, so 'model' gives T

indicators.note: in says the soldier is placed inside the rearranged car
broken-down says the letters of the word car are knocked out of order

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A gloomy tale of a fashion model and a soldier in a wrecked car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken-down' turns CAR into RAC; 'in' puts GI inside it to make RAGIC, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means deeply distressing, synonymous with sorrowful.

clue.text: Reacted differently when one sang another song

explanation.surface: A singer switched songs mid-performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to change one's opinion; literally, a singer switching to a different melody.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to alter one's opinion or attitude; taken literally it describes swapping one melody for another.

clue.text: An effort in the past

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: A try made long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means earlier than now, as in 'years before'.

clue.text: Series of actions by commander during the squeeze

indicators.note: during says the commander comes in the middle of the squeeze

parts.note: to press is to squeeze; a press is a squeeze
OC stands for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: An officer takes part in a crush of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts OC inside PRESS; 'by' just joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a sequence of steps taken toward an end.

clue.text: Trust in cleaner I licked into shape

indicators.note: something licked into shape is reorganised, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trusting a cleaner whom I have trained up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licked into shape' rearranges CLEANER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is dependence or confidence placed in someone.

clue.text: Large number of garden vessels

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a rockery is a garden of stones and alpine plants

explanation.surface: Lots of pots in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A rockery is a garden bed of stones and alpine plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery means plates, cups and dishes, the household vessels used for eating.

clue.text: One persisting with a gummed label

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps going, armed with a label.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is someone who perseveres, and also an adhesive label.

clue.text: Some take aim at the bird

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is needed: the letters run inside them

explanation.surface: A few people aim at a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes letters from inside 'take aim'.
explanation.definitionFit: The kea is a New Zealand mountain parrot.

clue.text: Wandered but remained round the river

indicators.note: round says the word for remained wraps around the river's letter

parts.note: stayed means remained
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone drifted off yet stayed near the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts STAYED round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam off course, like a lost animal.

clue.text: Putting everything on the said fish in higgledy piggledy fashion?

parts.note: all means everything
over means on top of

indicators.note: said marks the next word as one heard rather than spelt

parts.note: plaice is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: Smothering a fish in toppings in a messy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' turns PLAICE, a flatfish, into the sound-alike PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes things scattered everywhere in disorder, which is what higgledy-piggledy means.

clue.text: Most unsatisfactory metals melted down

indicators.note: metal melted down is recast in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor metals being melted for scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted down' rearranges METALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamest means weakest or least convincing, as of an excuse.

clue.text: Cannot relocate in Chinese port

indicators.note: relocate means move about, so the letters change position

explanation.surface: Someone unable to move house within a Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocate' rearranges CANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Canton is the old Western name for Guangzhou, a major southern Chinese seaport.

clue.text: In the shack left a comb

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A comb was left behind in the shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' takes letters from 'shack left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackle is a steel comb for dressing flax, and also a cockerel's neck feathers.

clue.text: Claiming one's taking for granted

explanation.surface: Someone's claims rest on presumption.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming means taking on or laying claim to a role, and also supposing something true without proof.

clue.text: Smart little creature

explanation.surface: A clever small animal.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'fly' means sharp or knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is slang for shrewd and quick-witted, and a fly is a small winged insect.

clue.text: Tax levied for 31 days by the king of France

parts.note: October has 31 days, abbreviated OCT
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A levy raised for a month by a French monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An octroi was a local duty on goods entering a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: An octroi was a duty charged on goods brought into a town, especially in France.

clue.text: Medicine found on the wall?

explanation.surface: A remedy discovered on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a liquid medicine of suspended droplets, and also water-based wall paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulsion is an oily medicine suspended in liquid, and also a type of matt paint used on interior walls.
